column1: # Dormancy registry for the Prometheus alert rules in this chart.
# A rule that loads is not a rule that can fire. Every rule below references at
# least one series that does not exist on the live Prometheus, so its expression
# cannot become true. Sleeping is not automatically a defect -- a rule watching
# HPA objects that do not exist is correctly asleep -- but the reason has to be
# written down where the reader can find it:
#     rule <tab> absent_series (comma separated) <tab> reason <tab> why
# reason is a closed set:
#   object_absent     the object family is not deployed; the rule wakes with it
#   component_absent  the component the rule watches is not deployed -- a defect,
#                     not dormancy: what the rule protects does not exist either
#   feature_off       the feature is not configured (no remote write, ...)
#   collector_off     the exporter is up but this collector is not enabled
#   exporter_version  the source binary's version does not expose the family
#   series_renamed    upstream renamed/removed the series; the rule needs a fix
#   known_defect      a defect that is declared, with the fix named in why
#   lazy_counter      the counter is created on the first bad event; empty means
#                     none happened, not that the rule is dead
#   error_only_state  the family is exported only while the bad state exists
#   code_not_deployed the code that emits it is newer than the running image;
#                     the family appears with the next roll
# The last three are shared by every layer the witness reads (Prometheus, the
# in-process `infra_watch` rules); the seven above them are the ones a single
# layer can tell apart on its own.
# The witness reading (`scripts/host/cogneva-alert-rule-witness-reading.sh` in
# the private companion repository) treats an absent series without a row here as red.
# A row whose series is back (or whose rule is gone) is reported as stale and
# must be deleted -- the condition it describes is no longer true.
# Re-read 2026-10-19 02:20Z against Prometheus 3.14.0, kubelet v1.36.4+k3s1.
# These nine rules (six Alertmanager, three Prometheus notification) watched an
# Alertmanager this deployment does not run and will not run: the alert delivery
# path here is in-process rule evaluation -> the platform's `alerts` table -> the
# WebUI panel, not a second delivery chain with its own queue and receivers.
# Keeping guards for a component that is absent by design is not dormancy, it is
# a permanent declared defect -- `component_absent` is documented as a defect.
# So the rule groups are retired in the monitoring values
# (`deploy/k3s/observability/helm/kube-prometheus-stack-values-small.yaml`:
# `defaultRules.rules.alertmanager: false` plus the three Prometheus
# notification rules under `defaultRules.disabled`), and their rows are deleted
# from this registry -- a row for a rule that no longer exists is stale.
# The full profile (`PROFILE=full`) does run Alertmanager and keeps the rules;
# nothing in this registry is needed there because their series exist.
# --- feature_off (3 rules): no remote write is configured -------------------
PrometheusRemoteStorageFailures
column4: No remote_write is configured, so the remote-storage queue never registers its counters.

column1: PrometheusRemoteWriteBehind
column4: No remote_write target exists; there is no queue head to fall behind the tip.

column1: PrometheusRemoteWriteDesiredShards
column4: No remote_write target exists; shard sizing only runs once remote write is configured.

column1: # --- object_absent (3 rules): HPA and PDB objects do not exist --------------
KubeHpaMaxedOut
column4: No HorizontalPodAutoscaler exists in the cluster; correct dormancy, the rule wakes when one is created.

column1: KubeHpaReplicasMismatch
column4: No HorizontalPodAutoscaler exists; the replica mismatch this rule guards cannot occur.

column1: KubePdbNotEnoughHealthyPods
column4: No PodDisruptionBudget exists; correct dormancy, the rule wakes when one is created.

column1: # --- exporter_version (14 rules): the source version does not expose it -----
KubeJobNotCompleted
column4: kube-state-metrics v2 dropped the kube_*_labels families; kube_job_info carries only allowlisted labels, which are off. The name appears only inside an unless clause, so its absence does not stop the rule from firing: it only makes the label_excluded_from_alerts opt-out inert. Restore by widening the allowlist and rewriting the clause to kube_job_info.

column1: KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp
column4: Same removed family as KubeJobNotCompleted, and again only inside an unless clause, so filling-volume alerts still fire; the opt-out is inert until the allowlist carries the label and the clause reads kube_persistentvolumeclaim_info.

column1: KubePersistentVolumeInodesFillingUp
column4: Same removed family and same unless-only position as KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp; the inode rule fires, its opt-out does not.

column1: KubePodNotReady
column4: kube_pod_status_reason is exported per reason only while a pod carries one (SchedulingGated et al.); no series means no pod is gated, and the unless clause then excludes nothing while the rule still fires on its phase/ready side.

column1: KubeNodeEviction
column4: kubelet_evictions is an ALPHA counter labelled by eviction_signal, created on the first increment; no series means no eviction happened, and the rule fires as soon as one does. Not removed upstream.

column1: KubeletClientCertificateExpiration
column4: The certificate-manager family exists only while kubelet runs with --rotate-certificates; k3s leaves it off, so this is a config gap, not an upstream removal. Enabling rotation would expose it.

column1: KubeletClientCertificateRenewalErrors
column4: Same certificate-manager gate: emitted only with --rotate-certificates enabled.

column1: KubeletServerCertificateExpiration
column4: Same certificate-manager gate: emitted only with server certificate rotation enabled.

column1: KubeletServerCertificateRenewalErrors
column4: Same certificate-manager gate: emitted only with server certificate rotation enabled.

column1: # --- collector_off (5 rules): node-exporter collectors not enabled ----------
NodeBondingDegraded
column4: The bonding collector is enabled by default in node-exporter and this host runs it -- node_scrape_collector_success{collector="bonding"} reads 0 because the host has no /proc/net/bonding at all, not because the collector is off. No bond device exists, so the family is empty; it is exported as soon as a bond is created and the rule then reads it.

column1: NodeRAIDDegraded
column4: The mdadm collector is enabled by default and reads success=1 on this host; /proc/mdstat lists the personalities but no arrays, so the family is legitimately empty. Create an array and the series appear.

column1: NodeRAIDDiskFailure
column4: Same collector and same reason as NodeRAIDDegraded: mdadm runs (success=1) and exports per-disk state once an array exists; this host has none.

column1: NodeSystemdServiceCrashlooping
column4: The systemd collector is the one opt-in collector among the three: node_scrape_collector_success has no series for it at all, and enabling it needs --collector.systemd plus the host dbus socket mounted into the pod. Turning it on can make node-exporter fail to start, so it is a deployment decision, not a flip.

column1: NodeSystemdServiceFailed
column4: Same opt-in collector as NodeSystemdServiceCrashlooping; absent from node_scrape_collector_success means it was never asked to run.

column1: # --- error_only_state (1 rule): the family exists only while the state does --
KubeNodeUnreachable
column4: kube-state-metrics exports one series per taint, so this family is empty while no node carries one -- and the exporter is demonstrably up, because kube_node_spec_unschedulable from the same node spec collector reads 1 here. Absent is the state, not the collector: the taint that makes a node unreachable is what creates the series, and the rule reads it from that moment.
